chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Yahya al-Kahili, from Abu Ahmad al-Kahili, and I think I have seen him, said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a young girl, with whom there is no close kinship (mahram), who captivates me, so I carry her and kiss her. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'When six years have passed for her, do not place her on your lap.'
ai.seo_question: At what age should a father stop carrying his daughter on his lap according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, the narrator asks Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about the permissibility of kissing a young girl with whom he has no marital bond, to which the Imam replies that once she reaches six years of age, one should not place her on one's lap. This establishes a specific age of *bulugh* (maturity) for girls regarding physical intimacy and modesty (*haya*), distinguishing between permissible affection and the onset of sexual awareness. The ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that six is the threshold where a girl begins to be considered distinct in terms of modesty, even if full legal maturity (*rushd*) is reached later.
